IX.20, copy of the agreement at Andelot. Guntram retains the third part of Paris formerly held by Sigibert. Clauses on Cahors and Galswinth’s other cities.

summary.de: Sohn Chlothars I. Gregor nennt Reims als seinen Sitz bei der Teilung von 561. Im Vertrag von Andelot erscheint später sein einstiger Anspruch auf einen Teil von Paris.
summary.en: Son of Chlothar I. Gregory names Reims as his seat in the division of 561. A former claim to part of Paris subsequently appears in the treaty of Andelot.

sourceRefs.locator: II.43 and III.1. Clovis dies at Paris and is buried in the church of the Holy Apostles that he and Clotild had built. The four sons are named and their inheritance described as equal. III.1 gives no meeting place or list of seats.

summary.de: Sohn Chlodwigs und Vater Theudeberts. Gregor ordnet seinen Herrschaftssitz rückblickend Reims zu.
summary.en: Son of Clovis and father of Theudebert. Gregory retrospectively associates his seat with Reims.

sourceRefs.locator: III.11. Chlothar and Childebert besiege Augustodunum. Godomar flees. Gregory links the siege with the acquisition of Burgundy.
Attestation 292. Gregory III.11, Latin and translation, siege of Autun and flight of Godomar. The record indexes the event under 534.

p. 23 and nn. 64–65. Marius of Avenches, Chronica s.a. 534 (MGH AA 11, p. 235), for the partition among Childebert, Chlothar and Theudebert. The author places the start of the siege in late 533 or early 534.

summary.de: Gregor nennt Autun als belagerte Stadt. Der Chronist Marius datiert den Übergang des burgundischen Königreichs in fränkische Hände.
summary.en: Gregory names Autun as the besieged city. The chronicler Marius dates the acquisition of the Burgundian kingdom by the Franks.

sourceRefs.locator: III.6 and III.18. The pursuit at Visorontia, Godomar’s recovery of his kingdom, Clotild’s care for the boys and the fate of Chlodomer’s sons. The call imitating the king’s men is Gregory’s account of his death.
Attestation 282. Gregory III.6, town identification, year 524 and named participants.
Écrans 3–7, printed pp. 19–22. Peat-bog find in 1870, battle of 524, the hypothetical identification with Chlodomer, gilding, six T-shaped bands and rivets.

summary.de: Bei Vézeronce-Curtin im heutigen Département Isère wird Gregors Visorontia verortet. Die Quelle nennt das Gebiet der Stadt Vienne.
summary.en: Gregory’s Visorontia is identified with the locality of Vézeronce-Curtin in present-day Isère. The text places it in the territory of Vienne.
